title: Nuclei Isolation From Murine and Human Periosteum For Transcriptomic Analyses
author: Simon Perrin
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Set up centrifuge
steps.instruction: Set the centrifuge to 4 °C and allow it to reach the set temperature before any use.

steps.title: Prepare RNase‑free solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare all solutions fresh on ice in RNase‑free conditions, using the exact compositions below.

substeps.instruction: Human sample collection medium (store ≤1 yr at 4 °C): 44.5 mL DMEM 1×, 5 mL HEPES 10 % (v/v), 0.5 mL Pen/Strep 1 % (v/v); total 50 mL.
70 % ethanol: 700 mL absolute ethanol mixed with 300 mL H₂O; total 1 000 mL.

Nuclei suspension buffer (make fresh, keep on ice at 4 °C): 0.5 mL RNase‑free PBS (10×) diluted to 1×, 0.1 g BSA (2 % w/v), 25 µL RNase inhibitor (40 U/µL) to achieve 0.2 U/µL, add RNase‑free water to 5 mL total.
DAPI buffer (make fresh, protect from light): 99 µL nuclei suspension buffer (1×) + 1 µL DAPI stock (5 mg/mL) for a 1/1 000 dilution; total 100 µL.

steps.title: Label tubes and ensure RNase‑free workspace
steps.instruction: Prepare and annotate all required tubes, pipettes, and dishes; work on a clean RNase‑free surface using RNase‑free consumables and reagents.

steps.title: Fresh murine periosteum isolation
steps.instruction: Isolate periosteum from at least five adult mice (8–12 weeks) and process immediately for nuclei extraction.

substeps.instruction: Sacrifice mice by cervical dislocation (or approved method).
Rinse limbs with 70 % ethanol.
Incise skin, remove it completely, cut at knee and ankle to detach tibias, and place tibias in a 100 mm sterile Petri dish containing RNase‑free chilled PBS on ice.
Remove surrounding soft tissue with forceps and scissors, taking care not to detach periosteum.
Cut off epiphyses and flush bone marrow with RNase‑free ice‑cold PBS.
Scrape periosteum from cortex with a dissecting chisel; collect tissue in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing ice‑cold lysis buffer and keep on ice.
Transfer tissue to a 100 mm sterile Petri dish with a drop of ice‑cold lysis buffer and chop with clean scissors until very small pieces are obtained.
Proceed immediately to nuclei extraction (step 7).

steps.title: Fracture callus isolation
steps.instruction: Induce tibial fracture in mice, collect fracture hematoma/callus, and prepare tissue for nuclei extraction.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize mice intraperitoneally with 50 mg/kg ketamine and 1 mg/kg medetomidine; inject 0.1 mg/kg buprenorphine subcutaneously for analgesia.
After 15–30 min, confirm adequate anesthesia, shave the right limb, and disinfect the skin.
Make a 2 cm skin incision along the tibia, expose the bone by gently separating muscles.
Drill three 0.4 mm holes perpendicular to the tibial axis in the mid‑diaphysis.
Create an osteotomy by cutting the bone along the three holes with scissors.
Close the skin wound with sutures.
Revive the mouse with 1 mg/kg atipamezole intraperitoneally and place on a 37 °C heating pad; give additional buprenorphine 0.1 mg/kg subcutaneously at 12 h and 24 h post‑surgery.

At the chosen post‑fracture time point (≤7 days), sacrifice mice, rinse limbs with 70 % ethanol, incise skin, remove it, and detach tibia at knee and ankle; place tibia in a 100 mm sterile Petri dish with RNase‑free chilled PBS on ice, handling gently to avoid fragmenting the fragile fracture.
Remove surrounding soft tissue with forceps and scissors.
Scrape fracture hematoma/callus and activated periosteum with a dissecting chisel; collect tissue in ice‑cold lysis buffer on ice.
Add a drop of ice‑cold lysis buffer to the tissue, chop with clean scissors until very small pieces are obtained.
Proceed immediately to nuclei extraction (step 7).

steps.title: Frozen human periosteum processing
steps.instruction: Collect, freeze, assess RNA quality, and prepare human periosteum tissue for nuclei extraction.

substeps.instruction: Immediately after surgical collection, place periosteum in a tube containing ≥10 mL ice‑cold human sample collection medium; keep at 4 °C (process within 3 h, up to 4 h).
In a biosafety cabinet, transfer tissue to a sterile Petri dish, wash with RNase‑free ice‑cold PBS to remove residual medium and blood.
Using scissors, scalpel, and tweezers, remove any muscle, fat, or damaged tissue.
Cut periosteum into pieces ≥0.5 × 0.5 cm; briefly place pieces in a dry Petri dish to remove excess medium (store at least three pieces if possible).
Place each piece in a properly labeled freezing tube and plunge directly into liquid nitrogen for ≥5 min, then transfer tubes to a –80 °C freezer (samples stable for years).
If possible, extract RNA from one sample of the same batch using an RNeasy Mini Kit (or equivalent) and assess integrity on an Agilent TapeStation; only use samples with RIN > 6.5.
When ready for nuclei extraction, retrieve frozen tissue, keep the tube on dry ice, and do not allow thawing.
Place frozen tissue on an RNase‑free Petri dish on ice, add a few drops of ice‑cold lysis buffer, and chop with clean scissors until very small pieces are obtained.
Proceed immediately to nuclei extraction (step 7).

steps.title: Extract nuclei from tissue
steps.instruction: Lyse tissue and isolate nuclei using a glass douncer and sequential filtration and centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the prepared tissue (from steps 4‑6) to a glass douncer and add up to 7 mL ice‑cold lysis buffer.
Place the douncer on ice for 2 min.
While on ice, lower and raise pestle A gently 15–20 times, avoiding bubble formation; ensure resistance is low (if high, re‑chop tissue or adjust tissue‑to‑buffer ratio).
Lower and raise pestle B gently up to 10 times.
Filter the suspension through a 100 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL conical tube, then filter the flow‑through through a 40 µm cell strainer into a clean 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; carefully discard supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Add 1 mL ice‑cold nuclei suspension buffer, resuspend the pellet, and transfer to an RNase‑free Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge again at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; carefully remove supernatant.
Resuspend the final pellet in 200 µL ice‑cold nuclei suspension buffer; keep on ice for sorting.

steps.title: Sort nuclei
steps.instruction: Label nuclei, sort up to 150 000 SYTOX‑positive nuclei, and concentrate them for downstream use.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL SYTOX™ AADvanced™ (or DAPI as alternative) to the nuclei suspension to stain DNA.

Using a flow cytometer, sort up to 150 000 SYTOX‑positive nuclei with the appropriate gating strategy; collect sorted nuclei into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 0.75 mL ice‑cold nuclei suspension buffer (include unstained controls).
Centrifuge the sorted nuclei at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; carefully remove supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 50 µL ice‑cold nuclei suspension buffer.

steps.title: Count and assess nuclei
steps.instruction: Determine nuclei concentration and evaluate quality before sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Mix 5 µL of the nuclei suspension with 10 µL DAPI solution (5 mg/mL stock) in a 0.2 mL tube; adjust dilution if needed for optimal counting.
Transfer 10 µL of the stained suspension onto a Kova slide.
Examine under a fluorescence microscope (brightfield + fluorescence) to verify that only intact, round nuclei are present and to count nuclei; calculate concentration (aim for 700–1 200 nuclei/µL).
If debris or abnormal nuclei are observed, discard the preparation and repeat from step 7.

steps.title: Load nuclei for snRNA‑seq
steps.instruction: Proceed immediately to single‑nucleus RNA‑sequencing library preparation using the manufacturer’s protocol, ensuring the nuclei suspension is at 700–1 200 nuclei/µL.
